title: Permissions
subtitle: Human-in-the-loop approvals, RBAC/ABAC policy, and the identities and agent bindings behind every action.

breakGlass.title: Break-glass emergency access
breakGlass.caption: Time-boxed exceptions to dual-control. Every activation, use, revocation and post-review is permanent audit evidence; this surface is for accountability, not convenience.
breakGlass.forbiddenBody: You do not have permission to view break-glass grants or their immutable use trails.
breakGlass.activationStateUnknown: Activation is unavailable until the console can verify the current grant and review state.
breakGlass.activationBlockedUnreviewed: A previous grant is still unreviewed. Close it if active, then have a different user account complete its post-review before opening another emergency window.
breakGlass.activationHumanRequired: A system token cannot activate emergency access. Sign in as a human administrator with a stable identity.
breakGlass.activationHardwareRequired: Break-glass activation needs a hardware-verified (AAL3) session. Complete the WebAuthn or PIV step-up from Identity → Privileged login, then return here.
breakGlass.currentCaption: Who can bypass dual-control at this moment, for which actions, and until when.
breakGlass.noActiveHint: No governed action can currently proceed through break-glass.
breakGlass.scopeAll: All governed actions that permit an emergency path
breakGlass.useReviewPendingHint: {{count}} emergency uses require review. Examine every immutable trail entry before signing off.
breakGlass.reviewPendingHint: This grant must be closed and reviewed by a different user account before another can be activated.
breakGlass.historyCaption: Effective state, scope, use count, closure and independent post-review for every emergency window.
breakGlass.historyEmptyHint: Emergency grants will appear here if one is ever activated.
breakGlass.detailCaption: Grant lifecycle and immutable use trail.
breakGlass.trailCaption: Every action that proceeded without its approval quorum. These entries are append-only and cannot be edited or removed.
breakGlass.revokeBody: The emergency window closes immediately. The grant and all use evidence remain permanent, and post-review is still required.
breakGlass.reviewBody: Your note and identity become permanent audit evidence. Confirm that you examined the full use trail and that you did not activate this grant.
breakGlass.reviewNoteHint: Required — record what happened and whether every emergency use was justified.
breakGlass.reviewActiveBlocked: Review cannot begin while the grant is active. Revoke it or let it expire, then examine the complete use trail.
breakGlass.reviewHumanBlocked: Only a human administrator with a stable identity can complete the post-review. A system token cannot provide separation-of-duties evidence.
breakGlass.reviewSelfBlocked: Separation of duties: you cannot review a grant you activated. A different user account must inspect the trail and sign it off.
breakGlass.reviewSeparationDenied: This review was not accepted because the activator cannot review their own grant. Do not retry; ask a different user account to inspect the trail and complete the review.

activate.title: Activate break-glass emergency access
activate.body: Open a temporary, tightly scoped window only when the normal two-person flow cannot finish in time.
activate.warning: This bypasses dual-control for the actions in scope until the window expires, emits a critical finding, and requires a later review by a DIFFERENT user account than the one that activated it. It does NOT cover the irreversible actions — finalizing an offboarding, erasing data, releasing a legal hold, recovering the ledger — which have no emergency path around the second approver.
activate.reasonHint: Required and permanently audited. State the incident and why dual-control cannot complete in time.
activate.scopeHint: Choose all actions, one exact action, or a family matched by prefix.
activate.scopeAll: All governed actions that permit an emergency path
activate.exactActionHint: Enter the complete governed action identifier with no wildcard.
activate.actionPrefixHint: Enter the prefix; a trailing wildcard is added when the grant is sent.
activate.invalidScope: Use a non-empty action with no embedded wildcard; the resulting scope may be at most 128 characters.
activate.durationHint: From 1 second to the hard limit of 86,400 seconds. Default: 3,600.
activate.invalidDuration: Duration must be a whole number from 1 to 86,400 seconds.

breakGlass.activationRecordingRequired: Your session must be actively recorded. The server refuses activation otherwise (412) — start a recorded session first.

approvals.title: Approval queue
approvals.caption: Pending human-in-the-loop requests. Each approve, reject and cancel is a deliberate, audited decision recorded in the immutable decision trail.
approvals.subject: Subject
approvals.escalatedHint: This request passed its escalation window and was escalated.
approvals.emptyHint: When an action requires human approval it appears here for review.
approvals.emptyPendingHint: The queue is clear — nothing is waiting on a decision.
approvals.actorHint: Audit actor handle — never an email address. Identity is resolved from the directory, not shown here.

decide.approveBody: Your decision is recorded permanently in the immutable decision trail and counts toward the approval threshold.
decide.rejectBody: A single rejection terminates the request and is recorded permanently in the decision trail.
decide.noteHint: Optional — recorded permanently alongside your decision.
decide.notePlaceholder: Why you are approving or rejecting (optional)…
decide.sodHint: You cannot decide on a request you opened, and a token without a stable user cannot decide.

cancel.title: Cancel this approval request?
cancel.body: It will be withdrawn from the queue and marked canceled. Only the original requester or a tenant admin can do this.

sweep.title: Run the approval sweep?
sweep.body: It marks past-deadline requests expired and escalates requests past their escalation window, then emits the corresponding findings. Safe to re-run.
sweep.more: Pending requests remain unscanned — run the sweep again to finish.

newRequest.title: Open an approval request
newRequest.body: It will appear in the approval queue and require the configured number of human approvals before the action can proceed. A matching approval policy overrides the values below.
newRequest.subjectKindHint: What class of thing the action targets (optional).
newRequest.requiredApprovalsHint: Ignored if a matching approval policy applies — the policy is authoritative.

detail.title: Approval request
detail.trailCaption: The immutable, append-only record of who decided what, when. Read-only — it can never be edited or removed.

policies.title: Policies
policies.caption: ABAC deny rules and approval thresholds. An ABAC rule can only further-restrict access; it is the author’s declared intent, not proof of runtime enforcement.
policies.enforcementCaption: Whether a policy is actually enforced depends on the deployment — an enabled policy may be authored and audited but inert if its evaluator is not wired.
policies.name: Policy
policies.emptyHint: Author an ABAC deny rule or an approval threshold to govern matching actions.

policyEditor.name: Name
policyEditor.nameHint: A short, descriptive label for this policy.
policyEditor.kindHint: The policy type. It cannot be changed after creation.
policyEditor.abacRulesHint: Each rule further-restricts access. “Deny” is implicit and not editable — v1 only supports deny rules. A rule must select at least one of permission, verb, resource or principal kind.
policyEditor.confirmCreateBody: An enabled ABAC policy further-restricts access immediately; an enabled approval policy starts requiring human approvals for matching actions. Takes effect immediately.
policyEditor.confirmUpdateBody: If enabled, the change takes effect immediately on the authorization path / approval flow. Policy kind cannot be changed.
policyEditor.credentialWarning: That looks like a credential value. Policy rules carry references and selectors only — never a secret.

policyRemove.title: Delete this policy?
policyRemove.body: An ABAC deny policy’s restrictions will be lifted, or an approval policy will stop requiring approvals for its matching actions. This cannot be undone.

identities.title: Identities
identities.caption: The reconciled identity roster — who and what exists in the estate. Metadata is allow-listed by the backend; only safe fields survive.
identities.name: Name
identities.emptyHint: Identities appear here once a directory source is reconciled for this tenant.

resync.title: Resync the identity roster?
resync.body: It reconciles every identity and group for this tenant from the configured directory sources. Recorded in the audit trail.
resync.partial: {{failed}} source(s) did NOT answer and were skipped: {{providers}}. The counts above cover only the sources that did.
resync.noProviders: No identity providers are configured for this tenant — nothing was reconciled.

groups.title: Groups
groups.caption: Reconciled collections (groups, roles, policies) mirrored from a directory source.
groups.name: Group
groups.emptyHint: Groups, roles and policies appear here as directory sources are reconciled.

members.title: Group members
members.subtitle: Members of “{{group}}”.
members.transitiveHint: Transitive walks nested collections down to leaf identities and shows the nesting path.

bindings.title: Agent bindings
bindings.caption: How each agent maps to its non-human identity (NHI) — the bridge that attributes the agent’s actions in the access map.
bindings.sharedHint: This identity is bound to more than one agent — per-agent attribution is collapsed.
bindings.emptyHint: Bind an agent to an identity to attribute its actions in the access map.

bind.title: Bind this agent to the selected identity?
bind.body: All actions the agent takes will be attributed to this identity in the access map. Binding to an already-bound identity collapses per-agent attribution.

unbind.title: Unbind this agent?
unbind.body: The access map will stop attributing the agent’s activity to its identity. This is idempotent.

caveat.deny: A deny rule is the policy author’s declared intent — not proof that the rule is enforced at runtime.
caveat.enforcement: Enabled does not always mean enforced: the evaluator or directory providers may be unwired in this deployment.

computerUse.title: Computer-use governance
computerUse.description: Governance of Claude computer-use tool calls. The PEP audits each proposed action (click, type, screenshot, scroll) and applies deny-closed policy.
computerUse.sensitiveInput: Computer-use typed text contains sensitive content (DLP classes detected)
computerUse.responseBlocked: Response withheld: computer-use typed text contains sensitive content
computerUse.honesty: Enforcement is verified-deployed at the proxy only. A custom ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL evades it. Computer-use tools are client-side: the model proposes, the client executes.
computerUse.enterpriseRequired: Deep screenshot analysis (OCR + DLP) and timeline recording require the enterprise add-on.

projects.title: Claude Projects governance
projects.description: Inventory of Anthropic Organization Projects, membership, and project-scoped API keys via the Admin API.
projects.missingOrgId: Projects connector has an API key but no organization_id configured — project inventory is disabled
projects.coverageGaps: Knowledge files, custom instructions and artifacts are not available via the Admin API.
projects.retentionViolation: Artifact shared without prior archival (policy: require_archive_on_share)

agentRisk.caption: Per-agent risk and autonomy tier from observed signals. The effective tier is what enforcement reads — the operator override when set, otherwise the heuristic suggestion.
agentRisk.forbiddenBody: You do not have permission to view agent risk profiles.

signals.truncated: scan truncated — counts are a floor

classify.title: Classify an agent
classify.body: Compute the suggested risk tier from the agent's observed signals — access edges, findings and autonomy. Idempotent: it updates the suggestion and never changes an operator override.
classify.agentHint: The agent's unique ID — a canonical UUID. A name or external reference is not accepted.

override.title: Override the risk tier
override.body: The operator tier takes precedence over the heuristic suggestion and becomes the effective tier that enforcement reads. Clear it to fall back to the suggestion.
override.tierHint: Choose one of the four tiers, or clear the override to use the suggestion.

review.title: Mark this classification reviewed?
review.body: You accept the current effective tier as correct. Your identity and the time become permanent audit evidence.

routines.title: Routine policies
routines.subtitle: Cadence floors, concurrency caps, approval requirements, cron allowlists and blocked environments for Claude Code Routines. Overlapping policies compose most-restrictive-wins.
routines.enforcementCaption: These controls are enforced when a routine is declared and again at every fire. A disabled policy is stored but composes into nothing.

list.emptyCaveat: An empty list is also how a stored value that could not be read is shown, so this may be an unreadable column rather than one the operator authored.
list.unreadable: Unreadable — stored value could not be parsed
list.unreadableCaveat: The engine could not parse this stored column. Enforcement refuses such a policy outright, so it denies closed rather than allowing anything.

posture.title: Effective posture
posture.indeterminate: This resolution is indeterminate on the {{axis}} axis. Enforcement denies closed here — it is a refusal, not an absence of controls.
posture.none: No enabled policy governs this scope.
posture.stale: the scope above changed; resolve again
posture.supersededByIndeterminate: The values below are what composed so far. They are NOT the outcome: an indeterminate resolution is refused outright, whatever they say.
posture.noneIndeterminate: No policy was composed for this scope, and the resolution was REFUSED on an unanswerable axis — that is not the same as no controls applying here.

remove.title: Delete routine policy
remove.body: “{{name}}” will stop composing into the effective posture. Routines it constrained become subject only to the remaining policies.

editor.newDescription: The name and the scope are fixed at creation; everything else stays editable.
editor.editDescription: Name and scope are immutable — they are this policy’s operator-facing identity.
editor.name: Name
editor.scopeRefRequired: A workspace- or user-scoped policy needs its reference.
editor.tenantScopeRef: A tenant-scoped policy must not carry a reference.
editor.noFloorHint: No floor: a routine may fire at any frequency this policy allows.
editor.cadenceRange: The interval must be between {{min}} and {{max}} seconds, or the floor must be turned off.
editor.maxActiveHint: 0 means no cap. Caps at different scopes constrain different populations and are not merged.
editor.capRange: The cap must be 0 or a positive whole number.
editor.cronEmptyWarning: An empty allowlist denies every cron under this policy. That is the effect the engine applies.
editor.envsEmptyWarning: An empty blocklist blocks nothing. To block an environment, list it.
editor.unreadableWarning: The stored value could not be parsed, so this policy currently denies closed. Writing any list here REPAIRS the column and removes that refusal — only choose another option if that is what you intend.
editor.cronEntriesRequired: List at least one cron pattern, or choose the empty-allowlist option to deny every cron on purpose.
editor.envsEntriesRequired: List at least one environment, or choose the empty-blocklist option — which blocks nothing.

agentRisk.title: No agent risk profiles yet
agentRisk.description: Classify an existing agent to compute its suggested risk tier from observed access edges, findings and autonomy signals.

binding.title: No agent bindings yet
binding.description: Bind an agent to an existing or newly minted NHI so its actions can be attributed to that identity in the access map.

group.title: No directory groups reconciled yet
group.description: After a directory source is configured, resync the roster to reconcile its groups, roles, policies and memberships.

identity.title: No identities reconciled yet
identity.description: After a directory source is configured, resync the roster to reconcile its human and non-human identities for this tenant.

policies.title: No governance policies authored yet
policies.description: Author an ABAC deny rule or approval threshold; runtime enforcement still depends on the evaluator wiring in this deployment.

routinePolicies.title: No routine policies authored yet
routinePolicies.description: Create a routine policy to set cadence floors, concurrency caps, approval requirements, cron allowlists or blocked environments.

agentcoreExport.caption: Project this tenant's governance rules onto an AWS AgentCore policy engine as Cedar policies. Planning is a dry run that writes nothing; applying writes the plan you reviewed and is subject to governance approval.
agentcoreExport.modeDefault: Tenant default (as configured on the host)
agentcoreExport.modeActive: ACTIVE — the exported policies are enforced
agentcoreExport.modeLogOnly: LOG_ONLY — decisions are logged, not enforced
agentcoreExport.modeTenantConfigured: the mode configured for this tenant
agentcoreExport.modeHint: The mode is part of what apply writes, so a plan is only valid for the mode it was computed with. Changing it here discards the plan on screen.
agentcoreExport.planFailed: The plan could not be computed.
agentcoreExport.planChangedTitle: The plan changed — nothing was applied.
agentcoreExport.planChangedBody: Before writing, the engine planned again and got a different result, so the plan you reviewed no longer describes what would happen. Compute the plan again and review it before applying.
agentcoreExport.emptyBody: Compute a plan to see exactly which AgentCore policies would be created, updated or deleted. Nothing is written until you apply a plan you have reviewed.
agentcoreExport.noChanges: This plan makes no changes to the remote policy engine.
agentcoreExport.unsupportedTitle: Rules that could not be exported: {{n}}
agentcoreExport.unsupportedBody: These rules are NOT part of this export and will not reach AgentCore. Applying the plan does not carry them across.
agentcoreExport.confirmMode: This will be applied in {{mode}} enforcement mode.
agentcoreExport.confirmCounts: To create: {{creates}}. To update: {{updates}}. To delete: {{deletes}}.
agentcoreExport.pendingTitle: Waiting for approval — nothing has been written
agentcoreExport.pendingBody: Governance has not approved this export, so no policy was written to AgentCore. This is neither a success nor a failure.
agentcoreExport.pendingRetry: The reviewed plan is unchanged and stays on screen: apply it again once the approval is granted.
agentcoreExport.partialBody: The export was approved and executed, but some writes did not succeed. The remote engine has moved, so compute the plan again to see what is left.
agentcoreExport.applyFailed: The export could not be applied.
agentcoreExport.notWiredTitle: AgentCore export is not wired in this deployment
agentcoreExport.notWiredBody: No AgentCore exporter is configured for this tenant, so the engine declines the request. An operator enables it on the host by pointing this variable at the export configuration file:
agentcoreExport.notWiredCredentials: That file belongs to the operator and holds AWS write credentials. The console never shows, requests or edits it.

registerAgent.title: Register an agent identity
registerAgent.body: Creates a governed lifecycle row — or promotes an identity that already exists.
registerAgent.identityRefHint: The identity reference in the roster.
registerAgent.sponsorRefHint: Required. Must be a HUMAN identity already in the roster — the engine refuses anything else.

emerging.title: Emerging agent-identity standards
emerging.description: A design-toward registry: what we track, where it would plug in, and why it is not implemented.
emerging.noAccess: You do not have access to the identity registry.
emerging.verifiedAt: Revisions verified against primary sources in {{month}}. They move — treat this as a date, not a guarantee.

status.stable: Stable — a seam may target it
